title: Add agent tooling example with safe defaults (guardrails + structured logs)
author: Sabrina James
release_notes: Adds a production-minded agent tooling example with guardrails (max iterations, timeouts, tool validation), structured logs with redaction, and a minimal smoke test for tool-call parsing.
description: Context: As part of the RAG + agents quickstart workstream, we want examples that demonstrate “production-minded by default” patterns (safe defaults, guardrails, and operational hooks) without forcing users into a full template scaffold. This PR adds a new agent tooling example that shows (1) a bounded agent loop (max iterations + max wall time), (2) strict tool schema + tool output size limits, (3) resilient request settings (timeouts + retry/backoff for non-streaming calls; streaming is out-of-scope here), and (4) structured logs with correlation IDs and redaction. What’s included: - New example at examples/agents/tooling-safe-defaults/ with a small HTTP server exposing POST /agent/run and a couple of demo tools (search_docs + get_account_status). - Agent loop with guardrails: max_iterations (default 6), max_tool_calls (default 10), max_tool_output_bytes (default 32KB), per-request deadline (default 25s), and tool whitelist enforcement. - Tool validation: request->tool args validated against JSON schema (zod in TS); tool output is truncated and annotated if it exceeds limits; tool errors are wrapped in a typed error with user-safe messaging. - Logging: JSON logs (pino) with fields: level, ts, msg, redwood.request_id (if present), trace_id/span_id (if OTel is configured), agent.iteration, tool.name, tool.status, error.type. Logs redact API keys and obvious secrets by default. - README: setup, env var contract, “why these defaults”, and a troubleshooting section (401/429/timeouts/tool schema failures). - Minimal smoke test (node:test) that exercises: a) invalid tool args -> tool validation error path, b) tool exception -> user-safe error surfaced, c) max_iterations reached -> agent aborts with explicit reason. Config: Uses env vars consistent with the template conventions: REDWOOD_API_KEY (required), REDWOOD_MODEL (default: redwood/verified-small), REDWOOD_BASE_URL (optional), AGENT_MAX_ITERATIONS, AGENT_MAX_TOOL_CALLS, AGENT_MAX_TOOL_OUTPUT_BYTES, AGENT_DEADLINE_MS. Notes / non-goals: - This is an example (not the template). It intentionally avoids a full OTel collector setup; however, it propagates request IDs into logs and includes optional OTel hooks if users already have an SDK/collector. - No vector store / retrieval pipeline here; the focus is tool calling + safe loop controls. Illustrative snippet (agent loop guardrails): const maxIterations = cfg.maxIterations ?? 6; const deadlineAt = Date.now() + (cfg.deadlineMs ?? 25_000); for (let i = 0; i < maxIterations; i++) { if (Date.now() > deadlineAt) throw new AgentAbortError('deadline_exceeded'); ... if (toolCalls > maxToolCalls) throw new AgentAbortError('max_tool_calls_exceeded'); } throw new AgentAbortError('max_iterations_exceeded'); Follow-ups: - Once the template’s error taxonomy stabilizes, we should align error.type values in this example to match the template taxonomy exactly. - Consider adding a second example showing streaming + reconnect once the TS SDK streaming improvements land (tracked in ENG-4186).
commits: examples(agents): implement bounded agent loop + tool whitelist
examples(agents): add zod schemas for tool args and output limits
examples(obs): add structured logging w/ redaction + request-id propagation
examples(tests): add smoke tests for tool validation + abort conditions
docs(examples): README w/ safe defaults rationale + troubleshooting
review_conversation: Monica Patel (review): Can we make sure the defaults match the template safe-defaults doc (esp. iteration count + tool output cap)? Also please add an explicit abort reason surfaced to the user so it’s debuggable without reading logs. Sabrina James (author): Updated defaults to max_iterations=6 and max_tool_output_bytes=32768 and added AgentAbortError with reason codes max_iterations_exceeded/max_tool_calls_exceeded/deadline_exceeded returned as a structured response (HTTP 200 w/ {status:"aborted", reason:"..."}). Dana Lo (review): Tool schema validation looks good. One request: ensure we don’t log full tool arguments by default; some users will accidentally pass PII. Can we log only tool.name + arg keys unless DEBUG? Sabrina James (author): Done—logger now records tool.arg_keys and tool.arg_bytes (size) only. Full args are behind LOG_TOOL_ARGS=true and still go through redaction. Marcus Lin (security review): Please confirm REDWOOD_API_KEY never shows up in logs/errors and that README tells users not to commit .env. Also avoid shipping sample data that looks real. Sabrina James (author): Added redaction patterns for api keys/bearer tokens, ensured errors never include headers, updated README to include “Secrets” section + .env in .gitignore. Tools use dummy inputs only. Christine Wong (SRE review): Add a per-request deadline to avoid runaway loops under partial outages. Also please use jittered backoff for retriable API errors; otherwise thundering herd during 429 bursts. Sabrina James (author): Added deadline guard and jittered exponential backoff (max 3 attempts) for non-streaming model calls. Added README note on tuning concurrency when hitting 429. Monica Patel (final): Approving. This will be a good reference for the templates’ agent loop patterns.
timeline_notes: Initial PR opened with core loop + tools; updated after review to align defaults, reduce logging sensitivity, and add deadline/backoff + smoke tests. Squashed and merged after CI green.
